_comment: Trader research tracker. Only records that an independent party audited or that the trader published can be scored as evidence; anything else is a lead. Figures are copied with the date they were read and the page they came from. Strategy codes refer to trading_os/05_Backtesting/gtos_backtest/champions.py. Updated weekly by the scheduled research task; validate with: py tools/trader_research.py check

verification_levels.A: Audited real-money competition or regulator filing
verification_levels.B: Platform-certified track record (broker or fund platform)
verification_levels.C: Published method by the trader (book, paper); record not independently checked here

traders.name: Larry Williams
traders.record: 1987 World Cup Championship of Futures Trading: 11,376% net return ($10,000 to about $1.1 million)
traders.method: Volatility breakout from the open by a fraction of the prior range; Oops failed-gap pattern; Williams %R; COT positioning; seasonality.
traders.notes: Single-year competition result; the same contest also records large drawdowns. Treat the return as proof of method, not as a target.

traders.name: Andrea Unger
traders.record: World Cup Championship of Futures Trading winner 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2012 (672% in 2008, 115% in 2009, 240% in 2010)
traders.method: Several simple automated systems; start from robust breakout or reversal ideas such as a break of yesterday's high; confirm the average trade beats costs before adding leverage.
traders.notes: 2012 title per https://www.ungeracademy.com/ (only four-time winner). Returns came with high leverage in a contest format; size by our 0.25% rule, not by his.

traders.name: Kevin Davey
traders.record: World Cup Championship of Futures Trading 2005-2007: one first place and two second places; 148%, 107% and 112% annual returns
traders.method: Strategy factory: idea, preliminary test, walk-forward, Monte Carlo, incubation on live data, written rules for when to quit a system; several systems in several markets.
traders.notes: His contribution is process, not a setup: the incubation and quit rules are now part of the gate.

traders.name: Michael Cook
traders.record: World Cup Championship of Futures Trading winner 2007 (250%) and 2014 (366%)
traders.method: Position sizing to maximise returns, stops set by market structure, discretion layered on systematic signals.
traders.notes: Lead for position-sizing and stop-placement ideas; no testable entry yet.

traders.name: Linda Bradford Raschke
traders.record: Published setups in Street Smarts (1995, with Laurence Connors); trading record not independently checked here
traders.method: Turtle Soup: fade a new 20-period extreme when the earlier extreme was at least 3-4 bars old. Holy Grail: with ADX(14) above 30 and rising, buy the first pullback to the 20-period moving average.
traders.notes: Turtle Soup is the published, testable version of the 'liquidity sweep' idea already on our research list.

traders.name: Toby Crabel
traders.record: Published NR4, NR7 and opening-range research (1990); later ran a large systematic fund; fund returns not checked here
traders.method: Range contraction (NR7: narrowest range of the last 7 days) followed by an opening range breakout to catch the expansion.
traders.notes: Closest published cousin of our S-002 pre-New York range breakout; compare the two directly.

traders.name: Richard Dennis and the Turtles (rules by Curtis Faith)
traders.record: Turtle rules published by former Turtle Curtis Faith; returns not checked here
traders.method: System 1: 20-day breakout, 10-day exit, skip after a winner. System 2: 55-day breakout, 20-day exit. N = 20-day ATR; stop 2N; up to 4 units added every N/2.
traders.notes: Trend following holds trades for weeks; it fits the personal account more than a prop evaluation with daily loss limits.

traders.name: Paul Tudor Jones
traders.record: Called the 1987 crash; long-running macro fund; fund figures not checked here
traders.method: Defensive filter: 'My metric for everything I look at is the 200-day moving average of closing prices'; aims for 5:1 reward to risk; never average losers.
traders.notes: Needs 200 days of history before the filter allows any trade.

traders.name: Patrick Nill
traders.record: 2026 World Cup Championship of Forex Trading, annual division: 1st with 300.3% (1 January to 12 November 2026, subject to final audit)
traders.status: Watch: search for interviews after the contest ends
traders.notes: Live standings change daily; the weekly task refreshes the figure.

traders.name: Darwinex DarwinIA leaders
traders.record: July 2026 DarwinIA SILVER winner MOFQ: 7.32% month, 24.9% six-month return, -5.85% six-month drawdown; field median six-month return 10.29%
traders.method: Strategies are anonymous; useful as a benchmark for what certified, allocatable returns and drawdowns look like.
traders.notes: Realism check: allocated traders on a regulated platform run near 10% per six months with about 6% drawdown, not 300%.
